subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw allow SKILL.md metadata to register autonomous scheduled or event-triggered agent runs, and if so under what approval and trust boundary?
rationale: This changes an installed skill from passive instructions into a source of future autonomous execution, so code inspection cannot decide the product/security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design permissioned metadata first
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved metadata contract with explicit operator approval, provenance, revocation, ClawHub indexing rules, and tests before wiring scheduler registration.

options.title: Keep scheduling explicit
options.body: Leave autonomous runs in explicit cron or standing-order configuration and limit SKILL.md to documentation-only trigger descriptions for now.

options.title: Route through plugin APIs
options.body: Require a plugin-owned scheduling or lifecycle-hook API before any skill package can request autonomous execution.

recommendation.title: Design permissioned metadata first
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved metadata contract with explicit operator approval, provenance, revocation, ClawHub indexing rules, and tests before wiring scheduler registration.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touches both skill prompt metadata and cron-adjacent runtime surfaces involved in this decision.
